To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Fe-based metallic glasses have a superior performance in degrading organic contaminants in water.
Fe based glassy powders have outstanding efficiency in degrading organic pollutants in aqueous solution.

1) the metallic glass powder with a high Fe content can completely decompose the azo dye in a short time, 2) the high chemical performance is attributed to the metastable thermodynamic state and the unique surface topography of the metallic glass, and 3) the metallic glass is a promising functional material.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the degradation of organic contaminants in water using a new material - the Fe-based metallic glass powders (MGPs)

the development and application of metallic glasses as a new material for the degradation of organic water contaminants, especially azo dyes, by using the Fe based metallic glass powder (MGP) with a high content of chemically inactive metalloids.
the degradation of organic pollutants in water by metallic glass powders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Fe based metallic glasses are promising materials for the treatment of organic water contaminants.

the outstanding chemical activity of Fe-based metallic glass powder is due to the metastable thermodynamics of the glassy alloy, and the high surface energy and surface area, which are the intrinsic characteristics of metallic glasses.
the Fe based metallic glasses exhibit a high catalytic activity in degrading organic pollutants, which is superior to the conventional Fe based materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chemical performance of metallic glasses is not determined by the chemical compositions, but by the metastable thermodynamic and the particle surface characteristics.

the Fe-based metallic glass powder is a new type of efficient heterogeneous catalyst for rapid degradation of azo dye, and the metastable nature of the glassy structure is a crucial factor in determining the chemical performance of metallic glass.
the chemical activity of metallic glass is a function of its metastable thermodynamic state, which is a consequence of its amorphous structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metastable thermodynamic state of metallic glasses can be exploited in catalyzing chemical reactions, which is a completely new concept.
the metallic glass powder can degrade organic water contaminants much faster than the traditional metallic powder.
the metastable thermodynamic and surface topography of Fe-based metallic glass powder are responsible for its high catalytic activity in degrading organic pollutants in water.
